title: The Day the Sky Blew Up
narration: 30 June 1908. A fireball streaks over Siberia—then silence. No crater. Just 2,150 square kilometers of flattened forest. What hit Earth that day?
visual_goal: Aerial shot of dense Siberian forest, then a sudden bright flash from the sky. The forest flattens in a wave. Cut to black.

title: The Blast That Circles the World
narration: The shockwave traveled 1,000 kilometers. It circled the Earth twice. Energy? 10 megatons of TNT—185 times Hiroshima.
visual_goal: Global map with concentric circles expanding from Siberia. A red pulse radiates outward, looping twice around the planet.

title: Vanavara: 65 Kilometers of Lucky Survivors
narration: 65 kilometers away, the trading post of Vanavara felt the heat. Windows shattered. People thrown to the ground. Yet no one died.
visual_goal: Black-and-white photo of Vanavara post-explosion: shattered windows, debris. A man stumbles, looking up in shock.

title: The Night the Sky Glowed
narration: For two days, Europe and Asia saw a sky so bright, you could read a newspaper at midnight. Then—gone.
visual_goal: Time-lapse of a night sky over a European city. Stars fade into a luminous twilight, then return to darkness.
search_queries: Tunguska event two days bright sky

title: The Mystery That Remains
narration: No crater. No asteroid fragments. Just a 5-to-10-kilometer airburst. The sky exploded—and left no trace. What was it?
visual_goal: Aerial shot of the Tunguska site today: dense forest, no visible scar. A single tree stands bent at the top, like a witness.
